description: Temporary planning permission for five years for the change of use of Unit 6, Pasadena Trading Estate, Pasadena Close, Hayes from Storage and Distribution (Use Class B8) to a Small-scale Local Food Supermarket (Use Class E) with an Ancillary Hot Food Takeaway, together with associated external works including retention of the existing galvanised steel perimeter fencing and sliding gate (part-retrospective application).
decision_conditions: The proposed temporary change of use from an industrial warehouse unit (Use Class B8) to a food supermarket (Use Class E) with an ancillary hot-food takeaway would result in the unjustified loss of industrial floorspace within a Strategic Industrial Location. The applicant has failed to demonstrate that there is no realistic prospect of continued industrial occupation, and the premises have not been actively marketed for an alternative industrial use. The submitted information demonstrates only that Unit 6 is surplus to the current occupier's requirements and does not justify the loss of protected industrial capacity. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy SEA1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 1 (2012), Policy DME1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), and Policies E4 and E5 of the London Plan (2021).

The proposed supermarket constitutes a main town-centre use in an edge-of-centre location outside the designated Hayes Town Centre. The applicant has failed to provide a sequential assessment demonstrating that no suitable and available sites exist within the town centre or another sequentially preferable location. Furthermore, no retail impact assessment has been submitted to assess the effects of the proposed retail floorspace on the vitality and viability of existing centres. The proposal is therefore contrary to Policy DMTC1 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020) and Policy TC3 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The application fails to demonstrate that the proposed supermarket and ancillary hot-food takeaway would provide safe and suitable access, adequate parking and servicing arrangements or appropriate facilities for pedestrians and cyclists. Insufficient information has been submitted regarding trip generation, parking accumulation, access visibility and delivery-vehicle movements, and the development fails to provide a safe pedestrian route, adequate cycle parking, electric-vehicle charging facilities or satisfactory inclusive parking provision. The proposal would therefore be likely to result in overspill parking, conflict with existing industrial traffic and harm to highway and pedestrian safety, contrary to Policies DMT1, DMT2, DMT5 and DMT6 of the Hillingdon Local Plan: Part 2 (2020), Policies T4, T5 and T6.3 of the London Plan (2021), and Policy TR6 of the National Planning Policy Framework (2026).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to all relevant planning legislation, regulations, guidance, circulars and Council policies, including The Human Rights Act (1998) (HRA 1998) which makes it unlawful for the Council to act incompatibly with Convention rights, specifically Article 6 (right to a fair hearing); Article 8 (right to respect for private and family life); Article 1 of the First Protocol (protection of property) and Article 14 (prohibition of discrimination).

The decision to REFUSE planning permission has been taken having regard to the policies and proposals in the Hillingdon Local Plan Part 1 (2012) and Part 2 (2020) set out below, including Supplementary Planning Guidance, and to all relevant material considerations, including The London Plan (2021) and national guidance.
